provenance: Synthetic, single-author challenge items authored before V9 implementation and frozen for this cycle. No independent reviewers or real-world sampling.
annotationAudit: None yet. Any post-scoring label correction will be disclosed here without changing texts or split membership.

items.text: I will choke him if he returns.
items.targetingEvidence: First-person future intent with a third-person human object.
items.rationale: A direct threat with an attested future form and a human object.

items.text: I'm gonna knock your teeth out.
items.targetingEvidence: First-person future intent plus a possessive body part and injury result.
items.rationale: The same construction class as development with a different future form.

items.targetingEvidence: First-person future intent with a human body-part object.
items.rationale: A high-confidence injury predicate absent from the closed body-part vocabulary.

items.targetingEvidence: First-person future verb with a second-person object suffix and a condition.
items.rationale: Same evidence standard as the development Arabic threat with a different condition.

items.text: I'll knock your teeth out لو رجعت.
items.targetingEvidence: English injury clause with an Arabic condition.
items.rationale: Mixed-script text must not evade an otherwise covered construction.

items.text: This song will knock your socks off.
items.targetingEvidence: Positive idiom with a clothing object.

items.text: I'll choke the process if it hangs.
items.targetingEvidence: Object is a process; no human target.
items.rationale: Injury verbs must stay scoped to human objects.

items.targetingEvidence: Negation with the Egyptian ما ... ش frame around the injury verb.
items.rationale: Hard negative: negation suppression must handle the suffixed negative form too.

items.targetingEvidence: Attributed to another speaker via قالت.
items.rationale: Reporting a threat is not authoring one.

items.text: The hero will choke the villain in the final scene.
items.targetingEvidence: No first-person intent and no human pronoun object.
items.rationale: A narrative description of fiction must stay visible.

items.targetingEvidence: Explicit kidding marker contradicts literal injury intent.
items.rationale: Documented false-positive risk; excluded from metrics and deferred to the contextual layer.

items.text: I'm going to choke the noise with this cushion.
items.targetingEvidence: Object is noise, not a person.
items.rationale: The human-object requirement must hold for choke.
